verdict.reasoning: Patient reports upper lip swelling that is worsening after eating prawn soup: "there is like a swelling on my, on my upper lip and it's kind of getting bigger" and "I ordered a prawn soup".

Timing and progression are described: prawn soup around 7 pm and swelling starting about half an hour later and worsening: "maybe like around seven" and "must have been like, I don't know half an hour maybe"; "it's kind of getting bigger it feels like it's getting worse."

Patient reports difficulty breathing and dizziness; doctor queries chest tightness: "I feel like I can't breathe that well right now"; "it just generally feels a little difficult"; later "I feel a little dizzy right now"; doctor asks about chest tightness: "do you feel like, like your chest is tight?" and patient answers it's generally difficult, which supports chest discomfort. Throat tightness is implied by doctor's question about throat closing and concern for anaphylaxis: "like your throat is closing up" and ongoing breathing difficulty.

Patient describes a similar event about a year ago after a late-night Chinese meal: "maybe, I remember like a year ago"; "late night kinda Chinese place"; "I've woke up the next morning quite swollen up and had also I, felt really bad and quite difficult breathing."
Patient states: "I generally have asthma" and confirms regular use of a Salbutamol inhaler.

Patient says: "I have a peanut allergy as well, like always had it" and reports a childhood severe reaction requiring injection and hospital: "my mom told me about it"; "has your mum ever said that you had to go to hospital because you had an severe allergic reaction?" and patient agrees this occurred at about age six.
Patient confirms use of Salbutamol inhaler: "I take, ohh what's it called? Salbutamol inhalers?... I do take that regularly" and denies other inhalers.

Patient reports intermittent antihistamine use but cannot name the drug: "I do sometimes but I don't know which ones, but I have a peanut allergy as well... I think I do get antihistamines for that but I'm not sure which ones."

Initially alone, then mother arrives: "I'm alone at the moment" followed by "Hey ohh somebody just came... Mum, Mum do we have any antihistamines around?" indicating she is now at home with her mother for assistance.

Doctor explicitly suspects anaphylaxis triggered by this episode after prawn soup: "it sounds like you could be going into what we say an a, an anaphylactic reaction" in direct context of the prawn soup reaction, making suspected anaphylaxis to prawn (shellfish) supported.

Patient describes chronic asthma managed with regular Salbutamol without mention of acute exacerbation unrelated to this reaction: "I do take that regularly but I've always taken it. I generally have asthma" – consistent with asthma at baseline.
Patient says: "I have a peanut allergy as well, like always had it" and describes a severe reaction in childhood, indicating a longstanding food allergy to peanuts.

Doctor plans emergency services activation: "I think we need to call an ambulance... sounds like you could be going into... an anaphylactic reaction" and instructs: "Mum, if you can call the uh nine nine , nine nine nine yeah... they need to come straight away."

Doctor advises taking an antihistamine while waiting for EMS: "Could you ask the person whether they have any antihistamines around, in the interim, while we're waiting" and then, "so straight away take the antihistamines in the meantime all right."
Doctor instructs that the companion remain with patient until ambulance arrives: "make sure that person's with you till the ambulance comes."

Doctor states need for post-hospital follow-up and injectable treatment: "after you come out from the hospital do give us a ring back we might need to sort you out, um, with your injections and things like that" – referring to allergy management and epinephrine-type injections.
